It's not like they're picking your house and skipping two on either side of you. It's a presentation of statistics intended to make you feel special and exclusive.

The fact of the matter is that due to a number of infrastructure reasons, a good portion of the US population doesn't have access to any wired high-speed internet, and those houses are definitely included in that statistic. Once you factor in the additional houses where cable or DSL is available, but not currently fiber optic, you probably could slide the numbers around to make a "1 in 5" statement.

Also, note the wording of "has a choice". This can include households where geography and infrastructure aren't the issue but perhaps financial or other problems are arising (the house can get fiber, but the home can't). While I don't think this case actually exists, it also means that houses that don't have any options other than fiber are in the "4 of 5" as well as buildings where you don't have a say in your provider, such as apartment complexes or other situations where a landlord or property manager has said "Thou shalt use this provider".
